youtube.title: There's More Than Two Levels of Hell — spoken jazz noir: a calm voice, a piano, an upright bass
youtube.description:
Spoken-word jazz noir in D minor at 60 BPM: a calm, authoritative woman reads fifteen levels of hell like an official directory, over a sparse piano, an upright bass and a barely audible jazz kit. Dark comedy, deadpan, late-night piano bar.
Spoken word, 6:48. The levels start with cold coffee and end somewhere much quieter.

She announces every level with the same cadence and the same neutral authority, from level one to level fifteen. The lyrics get worse; the music stays almost aggressively pleasant, and it thins as the list goes down. The first six levels have both piano hands, the bass and the kit. From seven the left hand plays every other bar and the snare is gone. The lower levels are single keys over one bass note a bar. After a long piano interlude only a faint kick is left, and by level fifteen the piano has nearly stopped: two notes in seven bars, the bass holding under her. Every note is written, the piano answers in the gaps between her lines, and no two pauses are the same length. It ends on one unresolved piano note and a last low strum of the bass.

Words: written for this song. Voice: synthetic speech (Azure AI Speech), one clip per line, placed by hand on the beat; nobody's recorded voice is in it. Kit: GBS Jazz (Figure Drum Kits by tripjazz, Freesound, CC0). Piano: the public Strudel piano pack. Bass: a General MIDI acoustic bass soundfont.

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install. 

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/levels-of-hell.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/
